analysis.title: European Leaders: Equity recommendations
key_insights: UBS CIO sees Europe entering a phase of renewal, with earnings growth set to accelerate on fiscal expansion, policy reforms and structural drivers (AI, power and resources, longevity). It recommends a diversified approach across sectors.

The CIO Equity Selection List has 25 European names across five themes: Demographics and Consumers, Defence and Infrastructure, Financing structural reforms, Industry 4.0 and Automation, and Decarbonization. Benchmark is MSCI EMU.
No selection or weight changes this edition. Only the 'Why it is CIO Selected' texts were updated for Santander, Standard Chartered, Barclays, ING, Société Générale and Raiffeisen.
Effective 1 November 2026 CIO no longer rates or ranks equities (no Most Preferred or Least Preferred, no top picks). 'CIO Selected' is a designation, not a rating, and carries no price target.

Model portfolio theme weights: Financing structural reforms 31%, Industry 4.0 and Automation 22%, Decarbonization 18%, Demographics and Consumers 15%, Defence and Infrastructure 14%. Constituents within each theme are equal-weighted.

Industry 4.0: European manufacturing PMI reached 50 for the first time in three years. ASML is seen as defensive, with the market over-discounting cyclical fears. ASM International is levered to GAA and 2nm ALD and epitaxy. Infineon's data center revenue is expected to reach a mid-teens percentage of group revenue by FY27. SAP's AI-driven dislocation is viewed as an entry point.

Defence and Infrastructure: NATO target of 5% of GDP by 2035 (3.5% core plus 1.5% related). Rheinmetall is seen with double-digit annual earnings growth to decade-end, but news flow is expected to stay volatile. Airbus has a multi-year backlog. Rolls-Royce targets 2028 EBIT of GBP 3.6-3.9bn and FCF of GBP 4.2-4.5bn.

Financials: banks are the largest theme. Barclays reiterated 2026 targets (RoTE above 12%, income GBP 31.5bn) with CET1 at 14.2%. Standard Chartered raised its 2026 NII growth guide to about 4% and its RoTE target to about 14% from above 12%. Société Générale commits to returning 50% of earnings and sees 3Q26 beats in French retail and markets. Erste completed the 49% Santander Polska stake. Raiffeisen's Russia deconsolidation is treated as optionality.

Decarbonization and electrification: Enel plans about EUR 53bn capex for 2026-28, with 2026 EPS guidance of EUR 0.72-0.74. RWE targets a 12% EPS CAGR for 2026-31 and a EUR 1.32 DPS for FY26. Prysmian, Schneider, Legrand and Siemens Energy are leveraged to grid and data center demand. Siemens Energy trades at a discount to US peers.

Demographics and Consumers: Richemont trades at 20-year relative P/E lows versus peers, with Jewellery Maisons up 14%. Ferrari upgraded FY guidance after 3Q26, with an order book extending into 2028. Lonza is added to raise health care exposure after recent lag.

Holcim trades at 18.4x P/E, below its 15-year average, and UBS thinks guidance and consensus are too low. Sika is expected to benefit as the construction market passes its trough in 2026. Siemens is on a de-conglomeration path, with a planned 30% Healthineers spin-off.
Key stock-level risks flagged include semi-cap order push-outs, a data center capex slowdown, euro strength versus the dollar, US tariffs, Russia and sanctions exposure, and delayed defence orders.

market_movers.rationale: CIO Selected designation maintained with no rating or price target, valuation attractive on NTM EV/EBIT.

sector_views.rationale: Largest theme weight at 31%. Banks trade at valuation discounts with strong capital returns and improving returns.
PMI at 50 and AI and fiscal tailwinds support semis, software and automation.
Grid, data center and renewables investment drive utilities and electrical equipment.
NATO spending targets and equipment renewal give high visibility.
Increasing exposure to a lagging European health care sector, led by Lonza.

earnings_insights: Barclays: 3Q26 reported weaker than expected on softer FICC and banking fees, equities strong. Management reiterated 2026 targets of RoTE above 12%, income GBP 31.5bn and NII above GBP 13.7bn ex IB and head office.
Standard Chartered: 3Q26 reported, 2026 NII growth guidance raised to about 4% and RoTE target to about 14% from above 12%. Impairments materially below expectations.
Ferrari: 3Q26 reported with a further upgrade to full-year revenue guidance across all metrics.
Enel: company guidance for 2026 EPS of EUR 0.72-0.74 and 2028 EPS of EUR 0.80-0.82.
Holcim: 1H26 results above full-year guidance, UBS sees guidance too conservative.
Société Générale: 3Q26 reported beats in French Retail and Global Markets. Santander 3Q26 showed market-share gains in deposits and lending.

macro_indicators.interpretation: First reading at 50 in three years, signalling expansion in manufacturing.
Supports a multi-year European defence order cycle.
Needs private capital mobilization via the Savings and Investment Union, supportive for banks.

risk_factors: Euro appreciation versus the dollar (Airbus, Ferrari).
Semi-cap order push-outs if consumer or memory end-markets weaken.
Slowdown in data center capex (Schneider, Siemens Energy, Legrand).
Weaker capital-markets activity, credit deterioration, regulation and litigation for banks.
Delayed defence orders or spending shift to US firms.
Tariffs and trade war, Russia sanctions exposure.
vol_and_positioning: Rheinmetall and the defence sector are expected to see increased volatility given fluid news flow.
Raiffeisen shares are likely to remain volatile.
geopolitical: Russia-Ukraine conflict and NATO spending targets drive the European defence cycle.
Raiffeisen's Russian operation is being wound down, with deconsolidation possible.
Ferrari flags the length of the geopolitical situation and effect on Middle East demand.
US tariffs are a risk for Ferrari, Richemont and Prysmian.

tension_points.bull_case: Structural European defence spending lifts earnings growth to double digits annually through decade-end at attractive multiples.
tension_points.bear_case: Delayed orders, lower spending or a shift to US firms, plus unresolved financing, would raise volatility.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Delayed defence orders or spending shifting toward US firms.

tension_points.bull_case: ASML and ASM International benefit from AI, memory tightness and GAA and 2nm ramps, and ASML valuation is an entry point.
tension_points.bear_case: Deterioration in consumer semiconductor or AI memory end-markets can cause order push-outs or cancellations.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Order push-outs or cancellations from weaker end-market demand.

theme_stances.key_argument: Fiscal, monetary and structural support should accelerate European earnings, favoring a diversified selection.
theme_stances.evidence: Europe is entering a phase of renewal

theme_stances.key_argument: NATO targets and equipment renewal create a major multi-year defence and infrastructure investment cycle.
theme_stances.evidence: Europe is entering a major investment cycle in defense and infrastructure

theme_stances.key_argument: Banks trade at valuation discounts with improving returns and strong capital returns.
